GLOBAL STYLE: photoreal car-commercial action comedy, 35mm, Kodak 500T grain, night city after rain, wet asphalt reflections, sodium and neon light, real-time 1:1 speed, NO slow motion, NO CGI look. 9:16.
REFERENCES: @image1 = THE CAR: a gold 1960s-style coupé, vehicle appearance only, no badges. @image2 = THE DRIVER: identity and wardrobe only, ignore the backdrop — enormous charcoal waxed handlebar moustache with spiral tips that ALWAYS covers his mouth, black turtleneck, charcoal blazer. @image3 = THE PASSENGER: identity and wardrobe only — platinum buzz cut, round red-tinted glasses, ivory suit, exactly ONE silver stopwatch. @image4 = THE PRODUCT: the gold AURUM drink can, exact label. @image5 = THE POLICE CRUISER: vehicle appearance only, no real insignia, no readable text.
FIXED GEOGRAPHY: a long empty wet city boulevard at night; the ONLY vehicles are the gold coupé, one police cruiser always BEHIND it, and one delivery van in shot 4. The coupé always travels screen-left to screen-right or away from camera; the cruiser always follows behind in the same lane. No other traffic.
CAR PHYSICS: both cars weigh two tons and always behave like it — nose dives under braking, body rolls onto the outside wheels in turns, tyres grip visibly, contact shadows stay planted; in the handbrake turn the tail steps out and is caught — a realistic controlled slide, never arcade drifting. Wheels always rotate in the direction of travel.
EXACTLY NINE SHOTS AND EIGHT HARD CUTS — no more, no fewer, no extra inserts.
Shot 1 (0–1.5s): ground-level static crash camera, low front three-quarter: the gold coupé launches from standstill, rear squats, rear wheels spin with white tyre smoke; police lights flash in the far background. Hard cut.
Shot 2 (1.5–4.5s): high drone, smooth: the coupé races down the empty boulevard, the police cruiser about 50 metres behind with lights flashing. Hard cut.
Shot 3 (4.5–7.0s): camera hard-mounted on the hood looking in through the windshield: the moustached man drives with both hands, eyes forward; beside him the woman clicks her silver stopwatch once, dry half-smile; red-blue light sweeps across them from the rear window. Hard cut.
Shot 4 (7.0–10.0s): chase-car camera at bumper height 1 metre behind the coupé: it brakes, nose dives, then a handbrake turn 90 degrees into a narrow side street, tail steps out, thick tyre smoke; a delivery van at the corner brakes hard and stops safely. Hard cut.
Shot 5 (10.0–12.0s): static long lens: the police cruiser brakes hard into the same corner, nose dives, fishtails slightly and follows. Hard cut.
Shot 6 (12.0–15.0s): low chase-car camera behind the coupé on a straight street: ahead, one traffic light at an empty intersection turns from amber to red. Hard cut.
Shot 7 (15.0–19.0s): drone directly overhead, locked off: the coupé stops perfectly at the white stop line under the red light; the police cruiser stops right behind it, lights still flashing. Stillness. Hard cut.
Shot 8 (19.0–24.0s): static side long lens with both stopped cars in frame: the driver's arm reaches out of the coupé window holding a cold sweating gold AURUM can back toward the cruiser; the officer leans out of the cruiser window, takes it and cracks it open — a burst of fizz. Hard cut.
Shot 9 (24.0–30.0s): drone rising slowly: the light turns green; the coupé and the cruiser pull away slowly side by side, the officer sipping from the gold can; hold to end.
POSITIVE LOCKS: same car, same faces and wardrobe in every shot; the moustache always hides the driver's mouth; the car never changes colour or shape; screen direction never flips; the camera never passes through glass, walls or vehicles; nobody is hurt; no weapons; no readable text except AURUM on the can.
FORBIDDEN: floating cars, sliding without tyre contact, extra cars, duplicate cars, cars changing lanes randomly, morphing, extra fingers.
AUDIO: police siren whoop and tyre screech at 0.0s; engine at full roar dominant 0–15s; siren doppler throughout the chase; long tyre squeal at 8.0s; van horn at 8.6s; screeching brakes at 15.5s; then near silence 16–19s: two engines idling and a car indicator ticking; can crack and loud fizz at 21.5s; one stopwatch click at 27.0s; engines pulling away gently to the end. No music, no dialogue.
